The Court made the following:
 The Honourable Dr Justice Venkata Jyothirmai Pratapa
 Writ Petition No: 26976/2024
Order:

-
This Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of Constitution of India with the following prayer for:
"...pleased to issue a writ or order or direction more particularly one in the nature of writ of mandamus, declaring the action of Respondent No.4 in summoning the petitioners to the 4th Respondents Police Station and interfering in the petitioners civil disputes Sn further interfering in the petitioners life and personal liberty without there being any proceedings or reasonable cause against the petitioners, as illegal,
arbitrary, unconstitutional, unjust and violative of Article 14, 19 and 21 of the Constitution of India, consequentially direct Respondent No. 4 herein not to call the Petitioners to 4th Respondents Police Station and further not to interfere in the civil disputes of the petitioners and to pass..."
2. Heard Sri Kondepudi Dwaraka Ramesh, learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri P.Ajay Babu,
learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that it is a case of interference of police in the civil disputes.

4. Sri P.Ajay Babu, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home, on written instructions, would submit that based on the complaint lodged by Maganti Sireesha, respondent-police was registered a case against the petitioners and one B.Yashwant Kumar vide Cr.No.617 of 2024 U/Section 420 IPC dated 25.10.2024.
He would further submit that, the petitioners were called to the police station for preliminary enquiry, but the petitioners did not turn up for preliminary enquiry.
Except registration of the said crime, respondent police never threatened the petitioners or interfered in the civil disputes between the parties.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that, recording the same, the writ petition may be disposed of.
6. Recording the above said submissions, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
However, the police are directed not to interfere in the civil disputes between the parties except under due process of law.
There shall be no order as to costs.

As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
_________________________________________ Dr. JUSTICE VENKATA JYOTHIRMAI PRATAPA 02.01.2026
